summary.text:
We need implement FB_Task in CODESYS ST. Need reason semantics carefully. Need compile at most 3 attempts.

States IDLE, MOVING, COMPLETE, FAULT enum. Initially IDLE. Priority: Jam forces FAULT from any state; Belt and Complete false. With Jam FALSE, Reset returns any state to IDLE. Without Reset, FAULT latched. Stop aborts non-fault cycle to IDLE. In IDLE accept Start only if AtExit FALSE and enter MOVING. In MOVING, AtExit enters COMPLETE. COMPLETE held until Reset or Stop; Start alone does not clear. Belt true only MOVING, Complete only COMPLETE, Fault only FAULT. At most one transition per scan.

Need be careful post-state outputs observed at end same scan. Example step in jam: after step3 state Fault. Step4 Jam false Reset true -> IDLE outputs all false. Step5 Start true AtExit true from IDLE: Start accepted only AtExit false, so remain IDLE, outputs false. Good.

Step jam step2 from MOVING with Jam true Reset true -> FAULT. priority Jam.

Step jam step6 from IDLE Start true Stop true AtExit false -> Stop priority over Start, remains IDLE.

Implementation simplest CASE with priority.

Need one transition per scan. Jam forces Fault (unless already Fault, remains Fault) always. If Jam true: state := FAULT. Else if Reset: state := IDLE. Else case state. But note "Without Reset, FAULT is latched." If in FAULT and no Reset, remains. Stop aborts non-fault cycle to IDLE. Does Stop in FAULT with no Reset keep FAULT? Priority list has Latched fault before Stop, yes Fault stays. Reset with Jam false clears fault. So:

IF Jam THEN
 state := FAULT;
ELSIF Reset THEN
 state := IDLE;
ELSE
 CASE state OF
 IDLE:
   IF Start AND NOT AtExit THEN state := MOVING; END_IF
 MOVING:
   IF Stop THEN state := IDLE;
   ELSIF AtExit THEN state := COMPLETE;
   END_IF
 COMPLETE:
   IF Stop THEN state := IDLE; END_IF  // Reset handled above, Start doesn't clear
 FAULT:
   ; // latched
 END_CASE
END_IF

Outputs derived from state after transitions:
Belt := (state = MOVING);
Complete := (state = COMPLETE);
Fault := (state = FAULT);

Check simultaneous Stop and AtExit in MOVING: priority Stop over normal transition? Safety priority "Stop" before normal transition. They said at most one. Should Stop win? likely yes. In MOVING, if Stop TRUE and AtExit TRUE, which? "Stop aborts a non-fault cycle to IDLE." Safety priority lists Stop before normal transition. So Stop should win. Our ELSIF does Stop first. Good. In COMPLETE Stop -> IDLE. (Reset also). In IDLE Stop ignored.

Check P5: qMoving & AtExit & !Jam & !Reset & !Stop -> Complete & !Belt. Good. P4 idle start. Good.

Need define enum DUT maybe state internal. declaration must be FUNCTION_BLOCK FB_Task followed all VAR sections. Interface exact inputs outputs. Supporting objects DUT name kind DUT declaration (TYPE ...). Let's construct.

Could avoid enum by integer? Better enum E_TaskState. Supporting_objects declaration maybe:
TYPE E_TaskState :
(
    IDLE := 0,
    MOVING := 1,
    COMPLETE := 2,
    FAULT := 3
);
END_TYPE

Need ensure CODESYS syntax. supporting object kind "DUT". Implementation maybe empty string? Required name, kind, declaration, implementation; functions need return_type. DUT implementation "". Could omit implementation? spec says each with name, kind, declaration, implementation. Include.

Declaration:
FUNCTION_BLOCK FB_Task
VAR_INPUT
    Start : BOOL;
    Stop : BOOL;
    AtExit : BOOL;
...
END_VAR
VAR_OUTPUT
...
END_VAR
VAR
    State : E_TaskState := E_TaskState.IDLE;
END_VAR

Question CODESYS enum initializer qualified? E_TaskState.IDLE may work in CODESYS 3.5? Usually enum values can be referenced as E_TaskState.IDLE, yes. Or IDLE. Need avoid potential name collisions with "Complete" output and enum COMPLETE. Enum value COMPLETE uppercase, output Complete mixed case; CODESYS case-insensitive! That might cause collision: enum value COMPLETE vs output Complete? In CODESYS identifiers case-insensitive, so enum member COMPLETE and variable Complete conflict? Possibly compiler error "COMPLETE already defined". Safer name enum type values StIdle, StMoving, StComplete, StFault. But requirements say states IDLE, MOVING... likely internal names not interface. Use E_TaskState with values eIdle, eMoving, eComplete, eFault. Fine.

Need compile. Let's do first candidate.

One nuance: output Fault should be TRUE in same scan Jam applied. We derive after setting state. Good.

At scan Reset true Jam false in MOVING -> IDLE, belt false. Good.

At scan in IDLE with Start true AtExit true and no reset -> no transition. Good.

Potential P7: Fault -> G Fault or until condition. Since Jam persists? Our logic Jam true forces fault, Jam false Reset true clears. If Jam false Reset false, stays fault. If Jam true reset true, fault. Good.

Let's submit.
